catalog_quote: 7. ACCENT, This is almost invariable, and for nouns it is usually placed on the first syllable of the word when stripped of its alliterative prefix. For verbs it is on the first syllable of the root. Each alternate syllable, whether before or after this main accented one, receives a secondary accent. Sometimes in nouns the accent may seem to fall on the alliterative prefix, but that this is not the case will be seen on referring to § 10. This is owing to the elision of the vowel of the alliterative prefix, but where any seeming exception occurs to the rule here given the accent will be marked by the sign '. ... just as English rhythm is dependent on accent and not on length of vowels, so in Bobangi, rhythm depends on the places of accent and not on the raising or lowering of the tones of the vowels. ... [sec. 30(3)] Noo and nooki are enclitics and do not take a prefix in the true sense,…

audit.recode_to: Keep MORPHOLOGICAL (stem-initial accent per Whitehead 1899 sec. 7) but add Motingea 2010: 22-23 as supporting source and a caution: Bobangi is a H/L tone language (lexical and grammatical tone); the only modern description states no accent/stress; Whitehead's 'tones' (sec. 4) conflate vowel aperture and pitch, so his 'accent' is an impressionistic 1899 rhythmic-prominence report. If house convention codes tone languages whose only stress statement is a pre-tonological missionary one as TONAL-OR-PITCH-ACCENT, recode to tonal; otherwise no recode.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2010. Aspects des parlers minoritaires des lacs Tumba et Inongo: contribution à l'histoire de contact des langues dans le bassin central congolais. (ILCAA Language Monograph Series 5.) Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. xiv+251 pp. Ch. 2 'Notes de grammaire bobangi', pp. 15-52.
sources.quote: No accent/stress statement anywhere in the Bobangi phonology. p. 22: 'Il existe deux catégories de tons: tons simples et tons complexes. Tons simples. Il s'agit du ton bas et du ton haut... Valeur des tons. Les tons ont en bobangi une valeur à la fois lexicale et grammaticale.' p. 23: 'La syllabe bobangi est essentiellement ouverte ... V, CV, CSV.' p. 15 credits Whitehead 1899 as the first transcription of a Bantu language 'qui tienne compte à la fois de l'existence des tons et d'un système à sept voyelles'. Data: 120-sentence Hulstaert questionnaire dictated 2003 by a speaker from Bokangamoi
sources.locator: 2.2.4 Tons p. 22; 2.2.5 Syllabes p. 23; 2.3.3 Morphotonemes p. 26ff; TOC p. viii (no accent section)
sources.note: Only modern linguistic description of Bobangi phonology (tone-marked, 7 vowels, H/L tone with lexical+grammatical function); our record rests solely on an 1899 pre-tonological missionary grammar and cites no modern source; should be added as supporting source for the tone facts and for the absence of any modern accent statement.
